# qsu

> qsu (Quick & Simple Utility) is a lightweight utility library that provides the same set of frequently used helper functions in three languages: JavaScript/Node.js, Dart/Flutter and Python. The function names, arguments and behavior are intentionally identical across languages, so code can be moved between them without relearning the API.

Things worth knowing before answering questions about qsu:

- Every public function is named in `camelCase` in all three languages, including Python and Dart. This is deliberate and non-idiomatic, so that the API stays identical across languages.
- Not every function exists in every language. Each entry below lists the languages that actually implement it; do not assume parity that is not listed.
- Optional arguments are expressed as an options object in JavaScript, as **named parameters** in Dart, and as either a `dict` positional argument or keyword arguments in Python.
- In JavaScript, the `crypto`, `file`, `net` and `os` categories require a Node.js runtime and are imported from the `qsu/node` subpath, as does `logBox`. Everything else is browser-safe and imported from `qsu`.
- Documentation is available in English (`https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/...`) and Korean (`https://qsu.cdget.com/ko/reference/...`). Only the English URLs are listed below; prepend `/ko` for the Korean version of any page.
- 133 functions across 13 categories are documented. Installation: `npm install qsu` (JavaScript), `dart pub add qsu` (Dart), `pip install qsu` (Python).

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://qsu.cdget.com/introduction): What qsu is, and which languages it supports.
- [Installation](https://qsu.cdget.com/installation): Installation instructions for every supported language.
- [Installation: JavaScript/Node.js](https://qsu.cdget.com/installation/javascript): Install and import the npm package, including the browser-safe and `qsu/node` entry points.
- [Installation: Dart/Flutter](https://qsu.cdget.com/installation/dart): Install and import the pub package.
- [Installation: Python](https://qsu.cdget.com/installation/python): Install and import the PyPI package.
- [Reference](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference): Index of all utility functions.

## array

Array creation, sorting, sampling, deduplication and grouping.

- [arrCompact](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrCompact) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a new array with every falsy value removed. The rejected set is fixed across languages: `null`, `false`, `0`, the empty string and `NaN`.
- [arrCount](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrCount) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the number of duplicates for each unique value in the given array. The array values can only be of type `String` or `Number`.
- [arrDifference](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrDifference) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the values of the first array that are not contained in any of the other arrays. Values are compared by value, so nested arrays and objects are matched as well.
- [arrGroupByMaxCount](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrGroupByMaxCount) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Separates the data in the given array into a two-dimensional array containing only the maximum number of elements. For example, if you have an array of 6 data in 2 groups, this function will create a 2-dimensional array with 3 lengths.
- [arrIntersection](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrIntersection) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the values that are present in every one of the given arrays. The result is unique and keeps the order of the first array.
- [arrMove](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrMove) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Moves the position of a specific element in an array to the specified position. (Position starts from 0.)
- [arrPick](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrPick) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a random item from the given array. If the array is empty or is not an array, it returns `null`.
- [arrRepeat](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrRepeat) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Repeats the data of an `Array` or `Object` a specific number of times and returns it as a 1d array.
- [arrShuffle](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrShuffle) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Shuffle the order of the given array and return.
- [arrTo1dArray](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrTo1dArray) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Merges all elements of a multidimensional array into a one-dimensional array.
- [arrUnique](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrUnique) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Remove duplicate values from array and two-dimensional array data. In the case of 2d arrays, json type data duplication is not removed.
- [arrWithDefault](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrWithDefault) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Initialize an array with a default value of a specific length.
- [arrWithNumber](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/arrWithNumber) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Creates and returns an Array in the order of start...end values.
- [average](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/average) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the average of all numeric values in an array.
- [sortByObjectKey](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/sortByObjectKey) (JavaScript, Python): Sort array values by a specific key value in an array containing multiple objects. It does not affect the order or value of elements within an object.
- [sortNumeric](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/array/sortNumeric) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): When sorting an array consisting of strings, it sorts first by the numbers contained in the strings, not by their names.

## crypto

Hashing, base64, symmetric encryption and id generation. In JavaScript these functions require a Node.js runtime and are imported from `qsu/node`.

- [decodeBase64](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/decodeBase64) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Decodes an encoded base64 string to a plain string.
- [decrypt](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/decrypt) (JavaScript, Python): Decrypt with the specified algorithm (default: `aes-256-cbc`) using a string and a secret (secret).
- [encodeBase64](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/encodeBase64) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Base64-encode the given string.
- [encrypt](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/encrypt) (JavaScript, Python): Encrypt with the algorithm of your choice (algorithm default: `aes-256-cbc`, ivSize default: `16`) using a string and a secret (secret).
- [md5Hash](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/md5Hash) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts String data to md5 hash value and returns it.
- [numberHash](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/numberHash) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the specified string as a hash value of type number. The return value can also be negative.
- [objectId](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/objectId) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a random string hash of the ObjectId format (primarily utilized by MongoDB).
- [sha1Hash](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/sha1Hash) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts String data to sha1 hash value and returns it.
- [sha256Hash](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/sha256Hash) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts String data to sha256 hash value and returns it.
- [sha512Hash](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/crypto/sha512Hash) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts String data to sha512 hash value and returns it.

## date

Date validation, formatting and range calculation.

- [createDateListFromRange](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/date/createDateListFromRange) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Create an array list of all dates from `startDate` to `endDate` in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- [dateToYYYYMMDD](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/date/dateToYYYYMMDD) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the date data of a Date object in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- [dayDiff](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/date/dayDiff) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Calculates the difference between two given dates and returns the number of days.
- [isValidDate](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/date/isValidDate) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Checks if a given date actually exists. Check only in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.
- [today](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/date/today) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns today's date.

## file

File and directory inspection, path handling and I/O. In JavaScript these functions require a Node.js runtime and are imported from `qsu/node`.

- [createDirectory](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/createDirectory) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Creates a directory with the specified path. Ignores the operation if the directory already exists.
- [createFile](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/createFile) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Create a file of empty data. If the same file already exists, it is ignored.
- [createFileWithDummy](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/createFileWithDummy) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Creates a file with the specified size in bytes. A size of `0` creates an empty file, and a negative size raises an error.
- [deleteAllFileFromDirectory](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/deleteAllFileFromDirectory) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Deletes all files in the specified directory path. However, the directory is preserved.
- [deleteFile](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/deleteFile) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Delete files or directory in the specified path. If the file does not exist in the path, it is ignored.
- [getCopyFileName](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getCopyFileName) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): This function scans an array containing a list of names and displays an alternative name if any duplicates are found. If no duplicates are found, the names are returned as is.
- [getFileExtension](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getFileExtension) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the file extension from the given file path. An empty string value is returned for files without extension.
- [getFileHashFromPath](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getFileHashFromPath) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the file in the specified path as a value hashed by a specific algorithm. The default algorithm is `md5`. This method uses a `Promise` to return a valid hash value.
- [getFileHashFromStream](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getFileHashFromStream) (JavaScript, Python): Returns a file in a Node.js ReadableStream object as a value hashed with a specific algorithm. The default algorithm is `md5`.
- [getFileInfo](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getFileInfo) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns file or directory information as an easy-to-understand object.
- [getFileName](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getFileName) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the file name within the path.
- [getFilePathLevel](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getFilePathLevel) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Determine how many steps the current path is. The root path (`/` or `C:\`) begins with step 1.
- [getFileSize](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getFileSize) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Calculates the size of the file at the given path.
- [getParentFilePath](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/getParentFilePath) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the parent path one level above the given path.
- [headFile](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/headFile) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the first line of the specified text file path. The `length` argument is the total number of lines to print. Default is `1`.
- [isFileExists](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/isFileExists) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): If a file or directory exists at the specified path, it returns `true`.
- [isFileHidden](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/isFileHidden) (JavaScript, Python): Checks whether a file or folder in the specified path is a hidden file. Determines system hidden files for Windows and the presence or absence of a `.`(dot) for Linux and macOS or other operating systems.
- [isValidFileName](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/isValidFileName) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Determines whether the passed path or filename is using a system-accepted string (Also check the valid file length). Returns false if the name is not available.
- [joinFilePath](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/joinFilePath) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Combines paths for each operating system according to the given parameter values.
- [moveFile](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/moveFile) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Moves a file in the specified file path to another path.
- [normalizeFile](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/normalizeFile) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the file name within the path.
- [tailFile](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/tailFile) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the last line of the specified text file path. The `length` argument is the total number of lines to print. Default is `1`. The last line of newline characters is ignored.
- [toPosixFilePath](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/toPosixFilePath) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the given path as a path in POSIX format (usually used by Linux). For example, a Windows path will be converted to `/` instead of `\\`.
- [toValidFilePath](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/file/toValidFilePath) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Remove invalid or unnecessary characters in the path.

## format

Human-readable formatting and safe parsing.

- [duration](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/format/duration) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Displays the given millisecond value in human-readable time. For example, the value of `604800000` (7 days) is displayed as `7 Days`.
- [fileSizeFormat](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/format/fileSizeFormat) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the given file size (in bytes) as a human-readable string.
- [numberFormat](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/format/numberFormat) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the given number formatted for easy reading, including commas.
- [safeJSONParse](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/format/safeJSONParse) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Attempts to parse without returning an error, even if the argument value is of the wrong type or in `JSON` format. If parsing fails, it will be replaced with the object set in `fallback`.
- [safeParseInt](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/format/safeParseInt) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Any argument value will be attempted to be parsed as a Number type without returning an error. If parsing fails, it is replaced by the number set in `fallback`.

## math

Basic arithmetic over argument lists or arrays, and random numbers.

- [div](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/math/div) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns after dividing all n arguments of numbers or the values of a single array of numbers.
- [mul](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/math/mul) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns after multiplying all n arguments of numbers or the values of a single array of numbers.
- [numPick](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/math/numPick) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a randomly selected number between the min and max values.
- [numUnique](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/math/numUnique) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a unique number based on the current timestamp.
- [sub](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/math/sub) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns after subtracting all n arguments of numbers or the values of a single array of numbers.
- [sum](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/math/sum) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns after adding up all the n arguments of numbers or the values of a single array of numbers.

## misc

Function-level helpers that do not belong to another category.

- [console](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/misc/console) (Dart): Ensure that text is displayed in full without being truncated in Dart's `print`.
- [debounce](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/misc/debounce) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): When the given function is executed repeatedly, the function is called if it has not been called again within the specified timeout.
- [funcTimes](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/misc/funcTimes) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Repeat iteratee n (times argument value) times. After the return result of each function is stored in the array in order, the final array is returned.
- [logBox](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/misc/logBox) (JavaScript, Python): Prints the given values to the console as a bordered table, one row per argument, so that long or structured values stay readable.
- [sleep](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/misc/sleep) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Sleep function using Promise.

- [throttle](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/misc/throttle) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Limits how often a function may run: however many times the returned wrapper is called, the function itself runs at most once per `wait` window. The counterpart of `debounce`.

## net

Network requests. In JavaScript these functions require a Node.js runtime and are imported from `qsu/node`.

- [fetchData](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/net/fetchData) (JavaScript, Python): This function is used to make `node:fetch` easier to use while ensuring data is returned regardless of the response status.

## object

Object traversal, merging, flattening and conversion.

- [objDeleteKeyByValue](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objDeleteKeyByValue) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Deletes keys equal to the given value from the object data. If the `recursive` option is `true`, also deletes all keys corresponding to the same value in the child items.
- [objFindItemRecursiveByKey](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objFindItemRecursiveByKey) (JavaScript, Python): Returns the object if the key of a specific piece of data in the object's dataset corresponds to a specific value. This function returns only one result, so it is used to search for unique IDs, including all of their children.
- [objInvert](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objInvert) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a new object with the keys and values swapped. Values are converted to text because keys are always strings, and the later entry wins when two share a value.
- [objMapKeys](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objMapKeys) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a new object whose keys are the values returned by the callback. The callback receives `(value, key)` and the values are carried over untouched.
- [objMergeNewKey](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objMergeNewKey) (JavaScript, Python): Merge two object data into one object. The key to this method is to compare the two objects and add the newly added key data, if any.
- [objPickBy](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objPickBy) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a new object containing only the entries for which the callback returns `true`. The callback receives `(value, key)` and only the top level is inspected.
- [objTo1d](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objTo1d) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Merges objects from the given object to the top level of the child items and displays the key names in steps, using a delimiter (`.` by default) instead of the existing keys.
- [objToArray](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objToArray) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts the given object to array format. The resulting array is a two-dimensional array with one key value stored as follows: `[key, value]`.
- [objToPrettyStr](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objToPrettyStr) (JavaScript, Python): Recursively output all the steps of the JSON object (`JSON.stringify`) and then output the JSON object with newlines and tab characters to make it easier to read in a `console` function, for example.
- [objToQueryString](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objToQueryString) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts the given object data to a URL query string.
- [objUpdate](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/object/objUpdate) (JavaScript, Python): Changes the value matching a specific key name in the given object. If the `recursive` option is `true`, it will also search in child object items.

## os

Information about the machine the process runs on. In JavaScript these functions require a Node.js runtime and are imported from `qsu/node`.

- [getCpu](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/os/getCpu) (JavaScript, Python): This function returns the name of the CPU currently used by the system. Depending on the OS, the name may be incorrect or may not be retrievable.
- [getHostname](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/os/getHostname) (JavaScript, Python): Retrieves the host name of the current device. This is usually the name of the system that was automatically set on the desktop or changed by the user.
- [getMachineId](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/os/getMachineId) (JavaScript, Python): Gets the unique UUID of the current device. Throws an error if the value is not retrieved. Returns a `Promise` object, so use `await` or `.then()` to wait for the operation to complete and get the correct value.
- [getRamSize](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/os/getRamSize) (JavaScript, Python): Retrieves the total RAM size of the current device. Returns it as readable text including the unit. Decimal places are rounded up.
- [getSid](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/os/getSid) (JavaScript, Python): Gets the Security Identifier (SID) value for the current user on the device. Throws an error if the value is not obtained.
- [getUptime](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/os/getUptime) (JavaScript, Python): Returns the number of seconds the Node.js process has been running.
- [runCommand](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/os/runCommand) (JavaScript, Python): It returns the result that is output after entering and executing the command prompt command.

## string

String transformation, capitalization, trimming and truncation.

- [capitalizeEachWords](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/capitalizeEachWords) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts every word with spaces to uppercase. If the naturally argument is true, only some special cases (such as prepositions) are kept lowercase.
- [capitalizeEverySentence](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/capitalizeEverySentence) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Capitalize the first letter of every sentence. Typically, the `.` characters to separate sentences, but this can be customized via the value of the `splitChar` argument.
- [capitalizeFirst](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/capitalizeFirst) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts the first letter of the entire string to uppercase and returns.
- [deburr](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/deburr) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Replaces accented Latin letters with their unaccented equivalents, so `déjà vu` becomes `deja vu`. Covers the Latin-1 Supplement and Latin Extended-A blocks plus combining marks.
- [escapeRegExp](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/escapeRegExp) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Escapes every regular expression metacharacter in the given string, so the value can be dropped into a pattern and matched literally.
- [getGroupKeys](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/getGroupKeys) (JavaScript, Python): Returns a text key enclosed between the start and end characters in the given string. This can be useful for identifying template string keys in strings that follow i18n syntax.
- [getStrBytes](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/getStrBytes) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the number of bytes in the given string.
- [removeNewLine](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/removeNewLine) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Removes `\n`, `\r` characters or replaces them with specified characters.
- [removeSpecialChar](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/removeSpecialChar) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns after removing all special characters, including spaces. If you want to allow any special characters as exceptions, list them in the second argument value without delimiters.
- [replaceBetween](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/replaceBetween) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Replaces text within a range starting and ending with a specific character in a given string with another string. For example, given the string `abc<DEF>ghi`, to change `<DEF>` to `def`, use `replaceBetween('abc<DEF>ghi', '<', '>', 'def')`.
- [split](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/split) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Splits a string based on the specified character and returns it as an Array. Unlike the existing split, it splits the values provided as multiple parameters (array or multiple arguments) at once.
- [strBlindRandom](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/strBlindRandom) (JavaScript, Python): Replace strings at random locations with a specified number of characters (default 1) with characters (default \*).
- [strCount](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/strCount) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the number of times the second String argument is contained in the first String argument.
- [strRandom](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/strRandom) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns a random String containing numbers or uppercase and lowercase letters of the given length. A non-positive `length` returns an empty string.
- [strShuffle](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/strShuffle) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Randomly shuffles the received string and returns it.
- [strToAscii](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/strToAscii) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts the given string to ascii code and returns it as an array.
- [strUnique](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/strUnique) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Remove duplicate characters from a given string and output only one.
- [trim](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/trim) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Removes all whitespace before and after a string. Unlike JavaScript's `trim` function, it converts two or more spaces between sentences into a single space.
- [truncate](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/truncate) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Truncates a long string to a specified length, optionally appending an ellipsis after the string.
- [truncateExpect](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/truncateExpect) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): The string ignores truncation until the ending character (`endStringChar`). If the expected length is reached, return the truncated string until after the ending character.
- [uncapitalizeFirst](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/uncapitalizeFirst) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts the first letter of the entire string to lowercase and returns. The inverse of `capitalizeFirst`.
- [urlJoin](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/urlJoin) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Merges the given string argument with the first argument (the beginning of the URL), joining it so that the slash (`/`) symbol is correctly included.

- [words](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/string/words) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Splits a string into the words it is made of and returns them as an array. Anything that is neither a letter nor a digit separates words, and camelCase boundaries, runs of capitals and runs of digits are split as well.

## verify

Type, equality, range and format validation.

- [between](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/between) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns `true` if the first argument is in the range of the second argument (`[min, max]`). To allow the minimum and maximum values to be in the range, pass `true` for the third argument.
- [contains](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/contains) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns `true` if the first string argument contains the second argument "string" or "one or more of the strings listed in the array".
- [hasBadWords](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/hasBadWords) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns `true` when the given text contains one of the banned words. The word list comes entirely from the caller; this function does not ship one.
- [is2dArray](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/is2dArray) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns `true` if the given array is a two-dimensional array.
- [isEmail](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/isEmail) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Checks if the given argument value is a valid email.
- [isEmpty](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/isEmpty) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns true if the passed data is empty or has a length of 0.
- [isEqual](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/isEqual) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): It compares the first argument value as the left operand and the argument values given thereafter as the right operand, and returns `true` if the values are all the same.
- [isEqualStrict](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/isEqualStrict) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): It compares the first argument value as the left operand and the argument values given thereafter as the right operand, and returns `true` if the values are all the same.
- [isObject](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/isObject) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Check whether the given data is of type `Object`. Returns `false` for other data types including `Array`.
- [isTrueMinimumNumberOfTimes](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/isTrueMinimumNumberOfTimes) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns `true` if the values given in the `conditions` array are true at least `minimumCount` times.
- [isUrl](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/isUrl) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns `true` if the given data is in the correct URL format. If withProtocol is `true`, it is automatically appended to the URL when the protocol does not exist.
- [len](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/verify/len) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Returns the length of any type of data. If the argument value is `null` or `undefined`, `0` is returned.

## web

URLs, slugs, user agents and other web-oriented helpers.

- [generateLicense](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/web/generateLicense) (JavaScript, Python): Returns text in a specific license format based on the author information of the given argument. The argument uses the Object type.
- [getParsedInfoFromAddress](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/web/getParsedInfoFromAddress) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Parses an address string into its parts and returns them as an object. It handles ordinary web URLs as well as host-only addresses, IPv4, IPv6 (bare or wrapped in `[]`), and SSH-style connection strings that carry user information such as `ssh://user:pass@host:port`.
- [getSlug](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/web/getSlug) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Converts a string into a URL-friendly slug. The input is trimmed, split into words on whitespace and any existing `-`/`_` characters, and joined back together with the chosen separator.
- [isBotAgent](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/web/isBotAgent) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Analyze the user agent value to determine if it's a bot for a search engine. Returns `true` if it's a bot.
- [isMatchPathname](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/web/isMatchPathname) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): You can check if the URL path in the first argument value is matched against the second set of rules. The matching rules can take a string or an array of strings, where both arguments are paths that start with `/`.
- [isMobile](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/web/isMobile) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Checks if the current user is accessing from a mobile device via the User Agent string. This function returns `false` for tablet users.
- [removeLocalePrefix](https://qsu.cdget.com/reference/web/removeLocalePrefix) (JavaScript, Dart, Python): Removes the first-level path from a URL or pathname. Use this when you need a locale-free path in special cases in a URL that normally uses locale prefixes.

- [Changelog: Python](https://qsu.cdget.com/changelog/python): Release history of the PyPI package.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/jooy2/qsu): Monorepo containing all three packages and this documentation.
- [npm package](https://npmjs.com/package/qsu): JavaScript/Node.js distribution.
- [pub.dev package](https://pub.dev/packages/qsu): Dart/Flutter distribution.
- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/qsu): Python distribution.
